newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A stocks rise on optimism, B index flat.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A stocks rise on optimism, B index flat.

text.p: Shenzhen's A share index ended up on Thursday on investors' optimism over the market's medium outlook, but profit-taking pushed it off intraday highs, brokers said.
The A share index firmed 2.17 points or 0.58 percent to close at 379.57 after hitting a high of 384.90 on heavy turnover of 9.67 billion yuan, up from 7.40 billion yuan on Wednesday.
The B share index was unchanged at 151.74 points, with turnover falling slightly to HK$93 million from Wednesday's HK$97 million.
"Optimism over the market's medium-term outlook fuelled buying, given the stability of China's economic environment," an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said.
"But profit-taking emerged late in the session, pushing prices off intraday highs," he said.
Brokers said they expected indices to rise next week after some corrections.
On the B share market, property concern China Vanke Co was the top gainer, rising HK$0.24 or 3.97 percent to HK$6.29 on volume of 321,600 shares.
Conglomerate Shenzhen Zhonghao gained HK$0.07 or 1.68 percent to HK$4.23 on thin trade of 126,362 shares, the session's second best performer.
Refrigerator manufacturer Hefei Meilin traded most on volume of 1.82 million shares, slipping HK$0.04 to HK$6.26 on profit-taking, brokers said.
Automobile components producer Weifu Fuel Injection, the sharpest loser, slumped HK$0.09 to HK$4.81 with 177,200 shares changing hands.
On the A share market, refrigerator producer Shaanxi Changling advanced 0.33 yuan to 7.27 yuan on the day's heaviest volume of 27.18 million shares worth 198 million yuan.
Institutions bought the counter on anticipation of good 1996 results, brokers said.
